correctness.rationale: Block-by-block reconstruction yields the exact five square-zero equations. Every nonzero square-zero 2x2 block has rank one and q^2−1 options; two independent module-Hom spaces contribute q^s each, uniformly for every square-zero Z; the last 2x2 commutator has q^2 solutions since RW anticommutes with P. The image–kernel count of square-zero Z gives the closed sum. The argument works in characteristic two and s=0; C++ direct exhaustive checks of seven finite fields/dimension cases passed.

value.rationale: For two square-zero anticommuting generators the product becomes nontrivial first at rank two of the first generator; a rank-one generator forces annihilation. The theorem counts that entire first genuinely non-annihilating fixed-target stratum for all n and all prime powers and gives a surprisingly uniform fiber: the count is exactly a universal q-power times the complete square-zero-matrix census in dimension n−4. This is a natural representation-variety boundary invariant, not an arbitrary fixed parameter or trivial negative check.
